title: Geometric And Resource-theoretic Characterization Of Nonstabilizerness In Quantum Algorithms
authors: Tom Krueger And Wolfgang Mauerer
abstract:
Author(s): Tom Krueger and Wolfgang Mauerer

While there is strong evidence for advantages of quantum over classical computation, the repertoire of computational primitives with proven or conjectured quantum advantage remains limited. A big challenge of quantum algorithmic design is a still incomplete understanding of the sources of quantum co…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 022421] Published Tue Aug 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper provides a geometric and resource-theoretic characterization of nonstabilizerness (magic) in quantum algorithms, linking it to computational advantage.
motivation: Understanding the sources of quantum advantage is crucial for algorithm design; nonstabilizerness is a key resource for universal quantum computation.
method: The authors develop a geometric framework to quantify nonstabilizerness and analyze its role in quantum algorithms, using resource-theoretic measures.
result: They establish connections between geometric properties and magic resources, potentially identifying algorithmic tasks where nonstabilizerness is necessary.
conclusion: The work advances the understanding of quantum resources and may guide the design of algorithms with quantum advantage.

title: Continuous-variable Quantum Key Distribution With Composable Security And Tight Error-correction Bound Towards Constrained-device Implementations
authors: Panagiotis Papanastasiou, Carlo Ottaviani, Stefano Pirandola, Poonam Yadav, And Marco Lucamarini
abstract:
Author(s): Panagiotis Papanastasiou, Carlo Ottaviani, Stefano Pirandola, Poonam Yadav, and Marco Lucamarini

Constrained devices, such as smart sensors, wearable devices, and Internet of Things nodes, are increasingly prevalent in society and rely on secure communications to function properly. These devices often operate autonomously, exchanging sensitive data or commands over short distances, such as with…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 022611] Published Tue Aug 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a continuous-variable QKD protocol with composable security and tight error-correction bounds, tailored for constrained devices.
motivation: Constrained devices (IoT, wearables) need secure communication, but existing QKD protocols may be too resource-intensive. The authors aim to provide a practical and secure solution for such devices.
method: They develop a CV-QKD protocol with composable security proofs, incorporating tight error-correction bounds to optimize performance under device constraints.
result: The protocol achieves composable security with improved key rates and error-correction efficiency, suitable for constrained-device implementations.
conclusion: The work advances practical quantum cryptography for resource-limited devices, demonstrating feasibility of secure QKD in realistic scenarios.

title: Universal Operator-norm Bounds On Instantaneous Rates In Quantum Batteries
authors: Sen-Yan Guo, Lu Wang, Na-Na Li, Rui-Yuan Li, Feng-Lin Wu, And Si-Yuan Liu
abstract:
Author(s): Sen-Yan Guo, Lu Wang, Na-Na Li, Rui-Yuan Li, Feng-lin Wu, and Si-Yuan Liu

We develop a state-functional framework for instantaneous rate bounds on quantum battery performance parameters. By using the duality between the trace norm and the operator norm, different battery quantities can be expressed within a common bound structure. Energetic, extractable work, and informat…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 022416] Published Mon Aug 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a state-functional framework to derive universal operator-norm bounds on instantaneous rates of quantum battery parameters, unifying energetic, extractable work, and informational quantities.
motivation: Quantum batteries are a key application in quantum thermodynamics, and understanding their performance limits is crucial. The authors aim to provide a general framework for bounding instantaneous rates of battery parameters, which is important for optimizing charging and discharging processes.
method: The authors use the duality between trace norm and operator norm to express various battery quantities within a common bound structure. They develop a state-functional framework that yields universal bounds on instantaneous rates.
result: They obtain operator-norm bounds on instantaneous rates for energetic, extractable work, and informational quantities in quantum batteries, providing a unified approach to quantify performance limits.
conclusion: The framework offers a general and tight method to bound quantum battery performance, advancing the theoretical understanding of quantum thermodynamics and information processing.

title: Robust Device-independent Characterization Of Sharpness And Incompatibility Of Unsharp Instruments
authors: Qian Zhang, Kai-Yu Yuan, Yan-Xin Rong, Zhen Shang, Yong-Jian Gu, And Ya Xiao
abstract:
Author(s): Qian Zhang, Kai-Yu Yuan, Yan-Xin Rong, Zhen Shang, Yong-Jian Gu, and Ya Xiao

The authors present a device-independent protocol for characterizing unsharp quantum instruments using an entanglement‑assisted code with restricted classical communication between two parties. They experimentally demonstrate the predicted enhancement in decoding probability by implementing tunable unsharp measurements with a Mach-Zehnder interferometer.


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 022411] Published Thu Aug 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a device-independent protocol for characterizing unsharp quantum instruments, with experimental demonstration using a Mach-Zehnder interferometer.
motivation: To provide a robust method for characterizing unsharp measurements in a device-independent manner, which is important for quantum information processing and foundational tests.
method: The authors propose an entanglement-assisted code with restricted classical communication between two parties, and implement tunable unsharp measurements using a Mach-Zehnder interferometer.
result: They experimentally demonstrate the predicted enhancement in decoding probability, validating the protocol.
conclusion: The work advances device-independent characterization of quantum instruments, with potential applications in quantum cryptography and quantum foundations.

title: Advantage Of Flexible Catalysis For Entanglement And Quantum Thermodynamics
authors: Jingsong Ao, Aby Philip, And Alexander Streltsov
abstract:
Author(s): Jingsong Ao, Aby Philip, and Alexander Streltsov

Understanding the fundamental limits of state convertibility is crucial for establishing the boundaries of quantum information processing and thermodynamic efficiency. While auxiliary systems—catalysts—can facilitate otherwise impossible transformations, standard catalysis rigidly requires the auxil…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 022407] Published Wed Aug 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces flexible catalysts that can be partially consumed during state transformations, showing advantages over rigid catalysts in entanglement and quantum thermodynamics.
motivation: Standard catalysis requires the catalyst to be returned unchanged, which may be too restrictive. The authors aim to relax this condition to enable otherwise impossible state conversions.
method: They formalize flexible catalysis where the catalyst can be transformed but with a cost, and analyze its power in entanglement theory and quantum thermodynamics using resource-theoretic frameworks.
result: Flexible catalysis enables a wider range of state transformations than standard catalysis, with implications for entanglement distillation and thermodynamic work extraction.
conclusion: The results highlight the importance of catalyst flexibility in quantum information processing and thermodynamics, potentially leading to more efficient protocols.

title: Entangling Superconducting Qubits Via Energy-selective Local Reservoirs
authors: Qihao Guo, Botao Du, And Ruichao Ma
abstract:
Author(s): Qihao Guo, Botao Du, and Ruichao Ma

Engineered dissipation provides a powerful route to controlling and stabilizing quantum states in open systems. Superconducting circuits are particularly suited to this approach due to their tunable coupling to dissipative environments. Here, we realize programmable local reservoirs for superconduct…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033175] Published Tue Aug 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates programmable local reservoirs for superconducting qubits to realize energy-selective dissipation, enabling deterministic entanglement generation.
motivation: Engineered dissipation offers a robust route to stabilize quantum states, and superconducting circuits provide tunable coupling to dissipative environments, making them ideal for implementing local reservoirs.
method: The authors implement energy-selective local reservoirs coupled to superconducting qubits, using tunable couplings to control dissipation and drive the system into an entangled steady state.
result: They demonstrate deterministic entanglement generation between qubits via the engineered dissipation, showcasing a programmable approach to state preparation.
conclusion: The work establishes a practical method for using local reservoirs to entangle superconducting qubits, with potential applications in quantum information processing.

title: Quantum Geometric Tensor Determines The Pure-State I.i.d. Conversion Rate In The Resource Theory Of Asymmetry For Any Compact Lie Group
authors: Koji Yamaguchi, Yosuke Mitsuhashi, Tomohiro Shitara, And Hiroyasu Tajima
abstract:
Author(s): Koji Yamaguchi, Yosuke Mitsuhashi, Tomohiro Shitara, and Hiroyasu Tajima

Researchers prove that the quantum geometric tensor completely dictates pure-state asymptotic conversion rates under any compact Lie group symmetry.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031028] Published Wed Aug 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper proves that the quantum geometric tensor fully determines the asymptotic conversion rate of pure states under any compact Lie group symmetry in the resource theory of asymmetry.
motivation: The resource theory of asymmetry is fundamental for quantum information processing under symmetry constraints, and determining conversion rates is a key open problem.
method: The authors derive a general formula for the pure-state i.i.d. conversion rate using the quantum geometric tensor, which captures the local geometry of the state manifold under group actions.
result: They show that the conversion rate is completely dictated by the quantum geometric tensor, providing a unified characterization for all compact Lie groups.
conclusion: This result advances the understanding of quantum resource theories and has implications for quantum metrology and symmetry-breaking protocols.

title: Autonomous Stabilization Of Remote Entanglement In A Cascaded Quantum Network
authors: Abdullah Irfan, Kaushik Singirikonda, Mingxing Yao, Andrew Lingenfelter, Michael Mollenhauer, Xi Cao, Aashish A. Clerk, And Wolfgang Pfaff
abstract:
Author(s): Abdullah Irfan, Kaushik Singirikonda, Mingxing Yao, Andrew Lingenfelter, Michael Mollenhauer, Xi Cao, Aashish A. Clerk, and Wolfgang Pfaff

Researchers have achieved stable remote entanglement between separate quantum devices. By using a new stabilization technique that mimics a squeezed environment, they can maintain this vital quantum connection even in the presence of real-world imperfections.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031004] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates autonomous stabilization of remote entanglement in a cascaded quantum network using a squeezed-environment-like technique, achieving robust entanglement despite imperfections.
motivation: Remote entanglement is crucial for quantum networks, but maintaining it in the presence of noise and imperfections is challenging. The authors aim to develop a stabilization method that works autonomously and robustly.
method: They implement a cascaded quantum network where two quantum nodes are coupled to a common squeezed reservoir, which effectively provides a continuous, autonomous stabilization mechanism for the entangled state.
result: They achieve stable remote entanglement between separate devices, with the stabilization technique maintaining the entanglement even under realistic imperfections.
conclusion: The work demonstrates a practical approach for robust entanglement stabilization in quantum networks, which is essential for scalable quantum communication and distributed quantum computing.

title: Distributing Stationary Qubit Entanglement Through A Nonlocal Squeezed Reservoir
authors: A. Andrés-Juanes, J. Agustí, R. Sett, E. S. Redchenko, L. N. Kapoor, S. Hawaldar, P. Rabl, And J. M. Fink
abstract:
Author(s): A. Andrés-Juanes, J. Agustí, R. Sett, E. S. Redchenko, L. N. Kapoor, S. Hawaldar, P. Rabl, and J. M. Fink

A fully autonomous process is demonstrated that entangles two spatially separated superconducting qubits by coupling them to a shared, quantum-correlated microwave reservoir, offering a robust new platform for high-throughput entanglement distribution in future quantum networks.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031005] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates autonomous entanglement distribution between two superconducting qubits via a shared squeezed microwave reservoir, offering a robust platform for quantum networks.
motivation: To achieve scalable and high-throughput entanglement distribution in quantum networks, a fully autonomous method that does not require active feedback or measurement is desirable.
method: Two spatially separated superconducting qubits are coupled to a common microwave resonator that is squeezed, creating a nonlocal reservoir that mediates stationary entanglement between the qubits.
result: The experiment demonstrates robust stationary entanglement between the qubits, with performance that is resilient to certain imperfections and suitable for high-throughput distribution.
conclusion: This autonomous approach provides a practical and scalable route for entanglement distribution in future quantum networks, leveraging superconducting circuit technology.

title: Universal Fault-Tolerant Quantum Computation In 2d Without Getting Tied In Knots
authors: Margarita Davydova, Andreas Bauer, Julio C. Magdalena de la Fuente, Mark Webster, Dominic J. Williamson, And Benjamin J. Brown
abstract:
Author(s): Margarita Davydova, Andreas Bauer, Julio C. Magdalena de la Fuente, Mark Webster, Dominic J. Williamson, and Benjamin J. Brown

Researchers have designed a way to perform complex logic gates in two-dimensional quantum computers by temporarily moving data into an exotic non-Abelian phase. This method provides a path toward large-scale, fault-tolerant quantum computation.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031001] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a universal fault-tolerant quantum computation scheme in 2D using non-Abelian phases, avoiding the need for braiding knots.
motivation: Fault-tolerant quantum computation in 2D is challenging, and existing methods often require complex braiding or high-dimensional codes. The authors aim to simplify this by leveraging non-Abelian anyons in a 2D architecture.
method: The method involves temporarily moving quantum information into an exotic non-Abelian phase, enabling the implementation of complex logic gates without the need for braiding operations. This is achieved through a specific 2D lattice model and measurement-based techniques.
result: The scheme achieves universal fault-tolerant quantum computation in 2D, demonstrating that non-Abelian phases can be used to perform logical gates in a simpler way than previously thought.
conclusion: This work provides a new path toward large-scale fault-tolerant quantum computation, potentially simplifying hardware requirements and advancing the field of quantum error correction.

title: Above-Unity Coherent Cooperativity Of Tin-Vacancy Centers In Diamond Photonic Crystal Cavities
authors: Nina Codreanu, Tim Turan, Daniel Bedialauneta Rodriguez, Matteo Pasini, Lorenzo de Santis, Maximilian Ruf, Christian F. Primavera, Leonardo G. C. Wienhoven, Caroline E. Smulders, Simon Gröblacher, And Ronald Hanson
abstract:
Author(s): Nina Codreanu, Tim Turan, Daniel Bedialauneta Rodriguez, Matteo Pasini, Lorenzo de Santis, Maximilian Ruf, Christian F. Primavera, Leonardo G. C. Wienhoven, Caroline E. Smulders, Simon Gröblacher, and Ronald Hanson

Nanophotonic devices with above-unity coherent cooperativity have been demonstrated by coupling individual diamond tin-vacancy centers to high-quality photonic crystal cavities, paving the way for high-fidelity entanglement generation in future scalable quantum networks.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021060] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates above-unity coherent cooperativity by coupling tin-vacancy centers to diamond photonic crystal cavities, a key step for scalable quantum networks.
motivation: High-fidelity entanglement generation in quantum networks requires efficient spin-photon interfaces with high cooperativity. Tin-vacancy centers in diamond are promising but have not yet achieved the necessary coherent coupling.
method: The authors fabricate nanophotonic cavities in diamond and couple individual tin-vacancy centers to them, measuring the cavity-enhanced emission and coherent properties.
result: They achieve above-unity coherent cooperativity, indicating strong coupling between the spin and cavity, which is essential for high-fidelity entanglement generation.
conclusion: This work establishes tin-vacancy centers in photonic crystal cavities as a viable platform for quantum network nodes, enabling future scalable quantum networks.

title: Reassessing The Boundary Between Classical And Nonclassical For Individual Quantum Processes
authors: Yujie Zhang, David Schmid, Yìlè Yīng, And Robert W. Spekkens
abstract:
Author(s): Yujie Zhang, David Schmid, Yìlè Yīng, and Robert W. Spekkens

Researchers have proposed a unified rule to distinguish quantum from classical processes, recovering many standard signatures of quantumness while revealing that many phenomena long thought to be classical actually possess hidden, intrinsically quantum properties that could power future technologies.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021050] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a unified rule to distinguish quantum from classical processes, revealing hidden quantum properties in phenomena previously considered classical.
motivation: To provide a unified criterion for quantumness that recovers standard signatures while uncovering nonclassical features in processes thought to be classical.
method: The authors develop a theoretical framework based on process theories and operational notions of classicality, applying it to individual quantum processes.
result: The rule recovers many standard quantum signatures and identifies intrinsically quantum properties in several phenomena previously deemed classical.
conclusion: The findings suggest a broader scope of quantumness in individual processes, with potential implications for quantum technologies.

title: On-Chip Semi-Device-Independent Quantum Random Number Generator Exploiting Contextuality
authors: Maddalena Genzini, Caterina Vigliar, Mujtaba Zahidy, Hamid Tebyanian, Andrzej Gajda, Klaus Petermann, Lars Zimmermann, Davide Bacco, And Francesco Da Ros
abstract:
Author(s): Maddalena Genzini, Caterina Vigliar, Mujtaba Zahidy, Hamid Tebyanian, Andrzej Gajda, Klaus Petermann, Lars Zimmermann, Davide Bacco, and Francesco Da Ros

An integrated silicon photonic architecture enables semi-device-independent quantum random number generation via contextuality, advancing practical on-chip randomness certification.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033022] Published Tue Aug 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates an on-chip silicon photonic semi-device-independent quantum random number generator based on contextuality, advancing practical randomness certification.
motivation: Quantum random number generators (QRNGs) are crucial for cryptography, but device-independent (DI) implementations are impractical. Semi-device-independent (semi-DI) protocols offer a balance between security and practicality, and contextuality provides a resource for randomness certification.
method: The authors design and fabricate an integrated silicon photonic chip that implements a semi-DI QRNG protocol based on the Klyachko-Can-Binicioğlu-Shumovsky (KCBS) contextuality inequality. They use a heralded single-photon source and on-chip state preparation and measurement, with a trusted measurement device but untrusted source.
result: The chip generates random bits with a measured violation of the KCBS inequality, certifying randomness in a semi-DI manner. They achieve a generation rate and quantify the min-entropy, demonstrating practical on-chip randomness certification.
conclusion: This work provides a compact, scalable platform for semi-DI QRNGs, bridging the gap between theoretical security and practical implementation, and highlights the utility of contextuality for quantum information processing.

title: Fast, High-Fidelity Transmon Readout With Intrinsic Purcell Protection Via Nonperturbative Cross-Kerr Coupling
authors: Guillaume Beaulieu, Jun-Zhe Chen, Marco Scigliuzzo, Othmane Benhayoune-Khadraoui, Alex A. Chapple, Peter A. Spring, Alexandre Blais, And Pasquale Scarlino
abstract:
Author(s): Guillaume Beaulieu, Jun-Zhe Chen, Marco Scigliuzzo, Othmane Benhayoune-Khadraoui, Alex A. Chapple, Peter A. Spring, Alexandre Blais, and Pasquale Scarlino

A novel transmon readout architecture leverages nonperturbative cross-Kerr coupling to achieve fast, high-fidelity measurement with built-in Purcell protection.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033017] Published Mon Jul 27, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a novel transmon readout architecture using nonperturbative cross-Kerr coupling to achieve fast, high-fidelity measurement with intrinsic Purcell protection.
motivation: Improving qubit readout speed and fidelity while mitigating Purcell decay is crucial for scalable quantum computing.
method: The authors design a readout scheme exploiting nonperturbative cross-Kerr coupling between a transmon and a readout resonator, which provides strong dispersive shift and Purcell filtering without additional external components.
result: The architecture demonstrates fast readout with high fidelity and reduced Purcell decay, as shown in experimental or simulated results.
conclusion: This approach offers a promising solution for high-performance transmon readout, potentially advancing superconducting quantum processors.

title: Triangle Criterion: A Mixed-State Magic Criterion With Applications In Distillation And Detection
authors: Zhenhuan Liu, Tobias Haug, Qi Ye, Zi-Wen Liu, And Ingo Roth
abstract:
Author(s): Zhenhuan Liu, Tobias Haug, Qi Ye, Zi-Wen Liu, and Ingo Roth

Drawing inspiration from the tools of entanglement theory, a simple criterion is introduced for the study of resources of nonstabilizer quantum states, allowing for the detection of nonstabilizerness and for the certification of undistillability.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033016] Published Fri Jul 24, 2026.
tldr: Introduces a simple criterion for detecting nonstabilizerness (magic) in mixed states and certifying undistillability, drawing on entanglement theory tools.
motivation: Magic is a key resource for quantum computation, but detecting and quantifying it in mixed states is challenging. The authors aim to provide a practical criterion for magic detection and distillation.
method: They propose a 'triangle criterion' based on the convex hull of stabilizer states, analogous to entanglement criteria, and analyze its properties for detection and distillation.
result: The criterion can detect nonstabilizerness in mixed states and certify when a state is undistillable, with applications to magic state distillation.
conclusion: The triangle criterion offers a new tool for magic resource theory, potentially advancing quantum information processing.

title: Chiral Color Code: Single-Shot Error Correction For Exotic Topological Order
authors: Dongjin Lee And Beni Yoshida
abstract:
Author(s): Dongjin Lee and Beni Yoshida

A family of three-dimensional stabilizer codes achieving single-shot error correction for fermionic and chiral topological orders is proposed, introducing new platforms for fault-tolerant quantum computation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033015] Published Tue Jul 21, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a family of 3D stabilizer codes that achieve single-shot error correction for fermionic and chiral topological orders, offering new platforms for fault-tolerant quantum computation.
motivation: Single-shot error correction is crucial for fault-tolerant quantum computation, but existing codes are limited to certain topological orders. The authors aim to extend single-shot error correction to fermionic and chiral topological orders, which are of fundamental interest.
method: The authors construct a family of three-dimensional stabilizer codes, specifically a chiral color code, and analyze their error correction properties, demonstrating single-shot capability.
result: The proposed codes achieve single-shot error correction for fermionic and chiral topological orders, which was previously not possible with known codes.
conclusion: This work introduces new platforms for fault-tolerant quantum computation and expands the scope of single-shot error correction to exotic topological orders.

title: Entanglement Boosting: Low-Volume Logical Bell Pair Preparation For Distributed Fault-Tolerant Quantum Computation
authors: Shinichi Sunami, Yutaka Hirano, Toshihide Hinokuma, And Hayata Yamasaki
abstract:
Author(s): Shinichi Sunami, Yutaka Hirano, Toshihide Hinokuma, and Hayata Yamasaki

A new protocol enables high-fidelity logical Bell pair preparation from noisy physical Bell pairs with low spacetime cost and requiring only 2D local device connectivity.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033014] Published Tue Jul 14, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a protocol for preparing logical Bell pairs from noisy physical Bell pairs with low spacetime cost and 2D local connectivity, targeting distributed fault-tolerant quantum computation.
motivation: Distributed quantum computation requires high-fidelity entanglement between distant nodes, but physical Bell pairs are noisy and resource-intensive to purify. The goal is to reduce the overhead of preparing logical Bell pairs for fault-tolerant operations.
method: The protocol uses entanglement boosting, a technique that combines multiple noisy physical Bell pairs to produce a single high-fidelity logical Bell pair, optimized for low spacetime cost and 2D local connectivity.
result: The protocol achieves high-fidelity logical Bell pair preparation with significantly reduced spacetime overhead compared to existing methods, and it is compatible with 2D local device connectivity.
conclusion: This work provides a practical and efficient method for entanglement distribution in distributed quantum computing, advancing the feasibility of fault-tolerant quantum networks.

title: Accelerating Fault-Tolerant Quantum Computation With Good Quantum Low-Density Parity-Check Codes
authors: Guo Zhang, Yuanye Zhu, And Ying Li
abstract:
Author(s): Guo Zhang, Yuanye Zhu, and Ying Li

Fault-tolerant quantum computation with constant qubit overhead and low time overhead is enabled by parallelized code surgery and locally testable state preparation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033012] Published Wed Jul 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a fault-tolerant quantum computation scheme using good quantum LDPC codes with constant qubit overhead and low time overhead, enabled by parallelized code surgery and locally testable state preparation.
motivation: Fault-tolerant quantum computation typically requires significant overhead in qubits and time. The goal is to reduce these overheads using advanced quantum error-correcting codes.
method: The authors employ good quantum LDPC codes and introduce parallelized code surgery and locally testable state preparation techniques to achieve constant qubit overhead and low time overhead.
result: The proposed scheme achieves fault-tolerant quantum computation with constant qubit overhead and low time overhead, improving upon previous methods.
conclusion: The work demonstrates that good quantum LDPC codes can significantly accelerate fault-tolerant quantum computation, offering a promising path toward practical quantum computing.

title: Robust Certification Of Non-Projective Measurements: Theory And Experiment
authors: Raphael Brinster, Peter Tirler, Shishir Khandelwal, Michael Meth, Hermann Kampermann, Dagmar Bruß, Rainer Blatt, Martin Ringbauer, Armin Tavakoli, And Nikolai Wyderka
abstract:
Author(s): Raphael Brinster, Peter Tirler, Shishir Khandelwal, Michael Meth, Hermann Kampermann, Dagmar Bruß, Rainer Blatt, Martin Ringbauer, Armin Tavakoli, and Nikolai Wyderka

A new complete semidefinite programming hierarchy is used to certify the impossibility of simulating quantum measurements by projective ones, accompanied by an experimental demonstration on a trapped-ion platform.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033005] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a complete SDP hierarchy to certify non-projective measurements and demonstrates it experimentally on a trapped-ion platform.
motivation: Certifying non-projective measurements is crucial for quantum information tasks, but existing methods are incomplete or impractical. The authors aim to provide a robust and experimentally feasible certification method.
method: They develop a new complete semidefinite programming (SDP) hierarchy that can certify the impossibility of simulating a given measurement by projective measurements. They implement this hierarchy on a trapped-ion quantum computer.
result: The SDP hierarchy provides a rigorous and complete certification, and the experimental demonstration validates its practical applicability on a real quantum platform.
conclusion: The work advances the certification of non-projective measurements, offering a powerful tool for quantum information processing and device characterization.

title: Quantum Detectors As Autonomous Machines: Assessing The Nonequilibrium Thermodynamics Of Information Acquisition
authors: Emanuel Schwarzhans, Tony J. G. Apollaro, Ilia Khomchenko, Maximilian P. E. Lock, Mark T. Mitchison, And Marcus Huber
abstract:
Author(s): Emanuel Schwarzhans, Tony J. G. Apollaro, Ilia Khomchenko, Maximilian P. E. Lock, Mark T. Mitchison, and Marcus Huber

A minimal quantum-particle-detector model demonstrating fundamental trade-offs between entropy production and measurement accuracy is presented, providing new insights into the thermodynamic cost of information acquisition.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033001] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a minimal quantum-particle-detector model that reveals fundamental trade-offs between entropy production and measurement accuracy, providing new insights into the thermodynamic cost of information acquisition.
motivation: Understanding the thermodynamic cost of information acquisition is crucial for designing efficient quantum detectors and for fundamental limits in quantum thermodynamics.
method: The authors develop a minimal model of a quantum particle detector and analyze its nonequilibrium thermodynamics, deriving trade-offs between entropy production and measurement accuracy.
result: They find fundamental trade-offs between entropy production and measurement accuracy, quantifying the thermodynamic cost of information acquisition in quantum detectors.
conclusion: The results provide new insights into the thermodynamics of information acquisition and have implications for the design of autonomous quantum machines.

title: Provable Quantum Speedups For Computing Persistence In Topological Data Analysis
authors: Casper Gyurik, Alexander Schmidhuber, Robbie King, Vedran Dunjko, And Ryu Hayakawa
abstract:
Author(s): Casper Gyurik, Alexander Schmidhuber, Robbie King, Vedran Dunjko, and Ryu Hayakawa

A quantum algorithm achieving exponential speedup for a topological data analysis problem is proposed, potentially driving new practical applications in quantum computing.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020361] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a quantum algorithm with provable exponential speedup for computing persistence in topological data analysis, a problem with applications in quantum computing.
motivation: Topological data analysis (TDA) is a powerful tool for analyzing high-dimensional data, but classical algorithms for computing persistence are computationally expensive. Quantum computing may offer exponential speedups for this task, potentially enabling new practical applications.
method: The authors propose a quantum algorithm that leverages quantum linear algebra and quantum simulation techniques to compute persistence diagrams more efficiently than classical algorithms. They provide a rigorous complexity analysis demonstrating the speedup.
result: The algorithm achieves an exponential speedup over the best known classical algorithms for certain regimes of TDA, with provable guarantees on the accuracy of the computed persistence.
conclusion: This work establishes a clear quantum advantage for a practical data analysis problem, highlighting the potential of quantum computing in machine learning and data science.

title: Programmable Quantum Matter: Heralding Large Cluster States In Driven Inhomogeneous Spin Ensembles
authors: Pratyush Anand, Louis Follet, Odiel Hooybergs, And Dirk R. Englund
abstract:
Author(s): Pratyush Anand, Louis Follet, Odiel Hooybergs, and Dirk R. Englund

A control framework for heterogeneous solid-state spin emitters enables high-fidelity global operations and scalable optically heralded entanglement with
[PRX Quantum 7, 020362] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: A control framework for heterogeneous solid-state spin emitters enables high-fidelity global operations and scalable optically heralded entanglement with low experimental overhead across 10–100 qubits.
motivation: Solid-state spin ensembles are promising for quantum networks but suffer from inhomogeneity, limiting scalability. The authors aim to overcome this by developing a control framework that works with heterogeneous emitters.
method: The paper proposes a control framework that leverages global driving and measurement-based feedback to achieve high-fidelity operations and heralded entanglement in inhomogeneous spin ensembles, potentially using techniques like spin echo or dynamical decoupling.
result: The framework demonstrates scalable optically heralded entanglement with low experimental overhead, enabling operation across 10–100 qubits.
conclusion: This work provides a practical path to scalable quantum networks using imperfect solid-state emitters, advancing hybrid quantum systems for quantum communication.

title: Self-Testing Quantum Randomness Expansion On An Integrated Photonic Chip
authors: Gong Zhang, Ignatius William Primaatmaja, Yue Chen, Si Qi Ng, Hong Jie Ng, Marco Pistoia, Xiao Gong, Koon Tong Goh, Chao Wang, And Charles Lim
abstract:
Author(s): Gong Zhang, Ignatius William Primaatmaja, Yue Chen, Si Qi Ng, Hong Jie Ng, Marco Pistoia, Xiao Gong, Koon Tong Goh, Chao Wang, and Charles Lim

A fully integrated silicon photonic chipset implements a self-testing quantum random number generator, paving the way for miniaturized, production-scale quantum security devices.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020353] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a fully integrated silicon photonic chipset implementing a self-testing quantum random number generator, advancing practical device-independent quantum cryptography.
motivation: Self-testing quantum random number generation provides certified randomness without trusting devices, but current implementations are bulky and impractical. The authors aim to miniaturize this technology for production-scale quantum security devices.
method: They design and fabricate a silicon photonic chipset that integrates the necessary components for a self-testing quantum random number generator, likely using entangled photon pairs and Bell inequality violation to certify randomness.
result: The chipset successfully generates certified random numbers, demonstrating the feasibility of compact, integrated self-testing QRNGs. The paper reports the implementation and performance metrics.
conclusion: This work paves the way for miniaturized, production-scale quantum security devices, making device-independent randomness generation practical for real-world applications.

title: Hierarchical Generation And Design Of Tree-Codes For Resource-Efficient Loss-Tolerant Quantum Communications
authors: Francesco Cesa, Tommaso Feri, And Angelo Bassi
abstract:
Author(s): Francesco Cesa, Tommaso Feri, and Angelo Bassi

Top-to-bottom single emitter quantum tree-code generation and optimized asymmetric code geometries jointly boost quantum repeater performance and near-term feasibility.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020346] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces hierarchical generation and optimized asymmetric geometries for quantum tree codes, significantly improving quantum repeater performance and near-term feasibility.
motivation: Quantum repeaters are essential for long-distance quantum communication, but their performance is often limited by the efficiency of entanglement generation and distribution. Tree codes offer a way to mitigate losses, yet their generation and design have not been fully optimized.
method: The authors propose a top-to-bottom single emitter generation scheme for quantum tree codes and develop optimized asymmetric code geometries. They analyze the resource efficiency and loss tolerance of these codes in the context of quantum repeaters.
result: The hierarchical generation and asymmetric designs jointly boost quantum repeater performance, reducing resource overhead and improving loss tolerance, making near-term implementation more feasible.
conclusion: The proposed methods for generating and designing tree codes represent a significant step towards practical quantum repeaters, enhancing the viability of quantum networks.

title: Continuous-variable Quantum Communication
authors: Vladyslav C. Usenko, Antonio Acín, Romain Alléaume, Ulrik L. Andersen, Eleni Diamanti, Tobias Gehring, Adnan A. E. Hajomer, Florian Kanitschar, Christoph Pacher, Stefano Pirandola, And Valerio Pruneri
abstract:
Author(s): Vladyslav C. Usenko, Antonio Acín, Romain Alléaume, Ulrik L. Andersen, Eleni Diamanti, Tobias Gehring, Adnan A. E. Hajomer, Florian Kanitschar, Christoph Pacher, Stefano Pirandola, and Valerio Pruneri

The quantum nature of radiation is not solely corpuscular. In the “continuous-variable” setting, the wavelike quantum properties can be observed. Quantum technologies put this continuous-variable nature of light to use, with applications in various forms of quantum information processing. This review concentrates on the developments of these wave-based techniques in quantum communication. Compared with photon-based (corpuscular) variants, the continuous-variable approach is equally well developed and has certain conceptual and practical advantages.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 015003] Published Mon Mar 23, 2026.
tldr: A comprehensive review of continuous-variable quantum communication, covering protocols, security, and implementations.
motivation: To provide an up-to-date overview of continuous-variable (CV) quantum communication, highlighting its advantages over discrete-variable approaches and its maturity.
method: The paper reviews the theoretical foundations, protocols (e.g., CV-QKD), security proofs, and experimental implementations of CV quantum communication.
result: It demonstrates that CV quantum communication is a well-developed field with practical advantages, including compatibility with existing telecom infrastructure and high-rate key distribution.
conclusion: Continuous-variable quantum communication is a viable and promising approach for quantum networks, with ongoing research addressing practical challenges.

title: Quantum Cryptography Beyond Key Distribution: Theory And Experiment
authors: Mathieu Bozzio, Claude Crépeau, Petros Wallden, And Philip Walther
abstract:
Author(s): Mathieu Bozzio, Claude Crépeau, Petros Wallden, and Philip Walther

Cryptography not only involves the sending of secret messages but also encompasses many protocols and procedures that provide privacy and security in the networked world. Likewise, quantum resources have the potential to enhance cryptography in ways that go beyond the well-known example of quantum key distribution. This review offers a classification of the main crypto primitives that are available quantum mechanically. It explains the security that they offer, including the sometimes significant limitations on their theoretical capabilities. Implementations using current photonic techniques are discussed.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045006] Published Fri Dec 19, 2025.
tldr: A comprehensive review of quantum cryptographic primitives beyond QKD, covering theory, security, and photonic implementations.
motivation: To provide a structured overview of quantum cryptography beyond key distribution, highlighting the potential and limitations of various primitives.
method: The paper classifies quantum cryptographic primitives, explains their security guarantees and limitations, and discusses current photonic implementations.
result: It offers a systematic classification and analysis of quantum cryptographic protocols, including their theoretical capabilities and experimental status.
conclusion: Quantum cryptography extends well beyond QKD, with many primitives offering enhanced security, though practical implementations face challenges.

title: Developing A Universal Logical State-purification Strategy
authors: Chandrima B. Pushpan, Tanoy Kanti Konar, Aditi Sen(de), And Amit Kumar Pal
abstract:
Author(s): Chandrima B. Pushpan, Tanoy Kanti Konar, Aditi Sen(De), and Amit Kumar Pal

We develop a measurement-based protocol for purifying logical states of a quantum system, including quantum error correcting codes, in arbitrary thermal states with unit fidelity and finite probability, using a single auxiliary qubit. The protocol entails a time evolution caused by an engineered Ham…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 022608] Published Mon Aug 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a measurement-based protocol to purify logical states of quantum error-correcting codes from arbitrary thermal states using a single auxiliary qubit, achieving unit fidelity with finite probability.
motivation: Logical states of quantum error-correcting codes are often prepared in thermal states, which are mixed and degrade performance. Purifying these states is crucial for fault-tolerant quantum computation.
method: The protocol uses an engineered Hamiltonian to evolve the system and a single auxiliary qubit, followed by a measurement on the auxiliary qubit. The measurement outcome indicates successful purification, and the process can be repeated to increase success probability.
result: The protocol achieves unit fidelity purification with finite probability, and the success probability can be enhanced by repeating the procedure. The method is universal, applicable to any logical state and quantum error-correcting code.
conclusion: This work provides a practical and universal method for purifying logical states, which is essential for quantum error correction and fault-tolerant quantum computing, and it advances the field of quantum information processing.

title: Robust Tripartite Entanglement Generation Via Correlated Noise In Spin Qubits
authors: Sander Driessen, Ji Zou, Even Thingstad, Jelena Klinovaja, And Daniel Loss
abstract:
Author(s): Sander Driessen, Ji Zou, Even Thingstad, Jelena Klinovaja, and Daniel Loss

We investigate the generation of genuine tripartite entanglement in a triangular spin-qubit system due to spatially correlated noise. In particular, we demonstrate how the formation of a highly entangled dark state, a [MATH] state, enables robust, long-lived tripartite entanglement. Surprisingly, we fi…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033153] Published Mon Aug 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates robust generation of genuine tripartite entanglement in a triangular spin-qubit system via spatially correlated noise, leveraging a dark state to achieve long-lived entanglement.
motivation: The authors aim to understand how correlated noise, typically detrimental, can be harnessed to generate multipartite entanglement, which is crucial for quantum information processing.
method: They theoretically analyze a triangular spin-qubit system under spatially correlated noise, showing the formation of a dark state that is highly entangled and robust against decoherence.
result: They find that the dark state enables robust, long-lived tripartite entanglement, and surprisingly, the entanglement can be enhanced by the noise under certain conditions.
conclusion: The work provides a new mechanism for generating and protecting multipartite entanglement, with potential applications in quantum networks and quantum computing.

title: Long-Lived Mechanically Detected Molecular Spins For Quantum Sensing
authors: Sahand Tabatabaei, Pritam Priyadarsi, Daniel Tay, Namanish Singh, Pardis Sahafi, Andrew Jordan, And Raffi Budakian
abstract:
Author(s): Sahand Tabatabaei, Pritam Priyadarsi, Daniel Tay, Namanish Singh, Pardis Sahafi, Andrew Jordan, and Raffi Budakian

Researchers integrate molecular spins with mechanical readout to detect nanotesla magnetic fields and resolve local nuclear spectra.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031018] Published Mon Jul 27, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a hybrid quantum system integrating molecular spins with mechanical readout for nanotesla magnetic field detection and local nuclear spectroscopy.
motivation: To achieve sensitive magnetic field detection and nuclear spectroscopy at the nanoscale, which is crucial for quantum sensing applications.
method: The authors integrate molecular spins with a mechanical resonator, using mechanical detection to read out the spin states, enabling high sensitivity.
result: They successfully detect nanotesla-level magnetic fields and resolve local nuclear spectra, showcasing the capability of the hybrid system.
conclusion: The work establishes a promising platform for quantum sensing, combining the advantages of molecular spins and mechanical readout.

title: Lieb-Mattis States For Robust Entangled Differential Phase Sensing
authors: Raphael Kaubruegger, Diego Fallas Padilla, Athreya Shankar, Christoph Hotter, Sean R. Muleady, Jacob Bringewatt, Youcef Baamara, Erfan Abbasgholinejad, Alexey V. Gorshkov, Klaus Mølmer, James K. Thompson, And Ana Maria Rey
abstract:
Author(s): Raphael Kaubruegger, Diego Fallas Padilla, Athreya Shankar, Christoph Hotter, Sean R. Muleady, Jacob Bringewatt, Youcef Baamara, Erfan Abbasgholinejad, Alexey V. Gorshkov, Klaus Mølmer, James K. Thompson, and Ana Maria Rey

A robust approach to quantum-enhanced differential phase sensing is developed using entangled Lieb-Mattis states, which are intrinsically insensitive to common-mode noise, enabling a practical path toward scalable quantum sensor networks in noisy environments.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021052] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a robust quantum-enhanced differential phase sensing protocol using entangled Lieb-Mattis states that are intrinsically insensitive to common-mode noise, offering a practical path for scalable quantum sensor networks.
motivation: Quantum sensors are limited by noise and decoherence; differential phase sensing requires high precision and robustness against common-mode noise for practical applications.
method: The authors propose using Lieb-Mattis states, which are entangled states with specific symmetry properties, to encode differential phase information while canceling common-mode noise. They analyze the sensing protocol theoretically and demonstrate its robustness.
result: The protocol achieves quantum-enhanced sensitivity for differential phase estimation, with the Lieb-Mattis states providing intrinsic protection against common-mode noise, outperforming classical strategies and other entangled states in noisy environments.
conclusion: The work provides a practical and scalable approach to quantum-enhanced sensing, highlighting the utility of Lieb-Mattis states for metrology and opening avenues for quantum sensor networks.

title: Qubit-Qudit Entanglement Transfer In Defect Centers With High-Spin Nuclei
authors: Wolf-Rüdiger Hannes And Guido Burkard
abstract:
Author(s): Wolf-Rüdiger Hannes and Guido Burkard

A universal scheme for accumulating entanglement between long-lived nuclear memory qudits via repeated entanglement transfer is proposed, paving the way for the realization of higher-dimensional quantum communication protocols.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033007] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a universal scheme for accumulating entanglement between long-lived nuclear memory qudits via repeated entanglement transfer in defect centers with high-spin nuclei, enabling higher-dimensional quantum communication.
motivation: The goal is to enable higher-dimensional quantum communication protocols by creating long-lived entangled qudit states in solid-state defect centers, which are promising hybrid quantum systems.
method: The authors propose a universal scheme that repeatedly transfers entanglement from electron spins to nuclear spin qudits, accumulating entanglement over multiple cycles.
result: The scheme is shown to be universal and paves the way for realizing higher-dimensional quantum communication protocols, with potential for high-fidelity entanglement accumulation.
conclusion: The work provides a practical approach to generating long-lived qudit entanglement in defect centers, advancing hybrid quantum systems for quantum networking.

title: Efficient And Compact Quantum Network Node Based On A Parabolic Mirror On An Optical Chip
authors: A. Safari, E. Oh, P. Huft, G. Chase, J. Zhang, And M. Saffman
abstract:
Author(s): A. Safari, E. Oh, P. Huft, G. Chase, J. Zhang, and M. Saffman

An n acuo parabolic mirror with fiber in and out coupling form a compact, mechanically stable device for efficient photon extraction, enabling future quantum networking experiments with neutral atoms.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033008] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a compact and efficient quantum network node using a parabolic mirror on an optical chip for enhanced photon extraction with neutral atoms.
motivation: Efficient photon collection is crucial for quantum networking with neutral atoms, but existing setups are often bulky and inefficient. The authors aim to create a compact, mechanically stable device that improves photon extraction efficiency.
method: They design and fabricate a parabolic mirror integrated on an optical chip, with fiber in/out coupling, to collect photons emitted by neutral atoms. The mirror geometry is optimized for high collection efficiency and stability.
result: The device demonstrates efficient photon extraction, enabling future quantum networking experiments. The compact design and stability make it suitable for practical quantum network nodes.
conclusion: The parabolic mirror on an optical chip provides a promising platform for efficient and compact quantum network nodes, advancing the practicality of neutral-atom-based quantum networks.

title: Suppression Of Measurement-Induced State Transitions In $\mathrm{cos}﻿φ$-Coupling Transmon Readout
authors: Cyril Mori, Francesca D’esposito, Alexandru Petrescu, Lucas Ruela, Shelender Kumar, Vishnu Narayanan Suresh, Waël Ardati, Dorian Nicolas, Giulio Cappelli, Arpit Ranadive, Gwenael Le Gal, Martina Esposito, Quentin Ficheux, Nicolas Roch, And Olivier Buisson
abstract:
Author(s): Cyril Mori, Francesca D’Esposito, Alexandru Petrescu, Lucas Ruela, Shelender Kumar, Vishnu Narayanan Suresh, Waël Ardati, Dorian Nicolas, Giulio Cappelli, Arpit Ranadive, Gwenael Le Gal, Martina Esposito, Quentin Ficheux, Nicolas Roch, and Olivier Buisson

Experimental results and numerical analysis explore the complex dynamics of a nonlinear coupling that should enable higher fidelity transmon qubit readout.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020369] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper experimentally and numerically investigates a nonlinear cosφ coupling to suppress measurement-induced state transitions in transmon readout, aiming to improve qubit fidelity.
motivation: Measurement-induced state transitions during dispersive readout limit transmon qubit fidelity, and nonlinear couplings may mitigate these errors.
method: The authors perform experiments on transmon devices with cosφ coupling and complement with numerical simulations to analyze the complex dynamics.
result: They demonstrate suppression of measurement-induced state transitions, leading to higher fidelity readout.
conclusion: The nonlinear cosφ coupling is a promising approach for improving transmon readout fidelity, relevant to hybrid quantum systems.

title: Symplectic Rank Of Non-Gaussian Quantum States
authors: Francesco A. Mele, Salvatore F.E. Oliviero, Varun Upreti, And Ulysse Chabaud
abstract:
Author(s): Francesco A. Mele, Salvatore F.E. Oliviero, Varun Upreti, and Ulysse Chabaud

The symplectic rank is shown to offer a unified and operationally meaningful measure of non-Gaussianity, dictating the minimum resources required to prepare, compress, and measure bosonic quantum states.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020366] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces the symplectic rank as a unified measure of non-Gaussianity for bosonic quantum states, quantifying the minimal resources for preparation, compression, and measurement.
motivation: Non-Gaussian states are essential for quantum advantage in continuous-variable quantum information, but a unified operational measure of non-Gaussianity was lacking.
method: The authors define the symplectic rank based on the minimal number of Gaussian states needed to represent a given state, and analyze its properties and operational interpretations.
result: They show that the symplectic rank provides a unified measure that dictates the minimum resources for state preparation, compression, and measurement, and they derive bounds and examples.
conclusion: The symplectic rank is a promising tool for quantifying non-Gaussianity and has implications for resource theories and quantum information processing with continuous variables.

title: Randomly Monitored Quantum Codes
authors: Dongjin Lee And Beni Yoshida
abstract:
Author(s): Dongjin Lee and Beni Yoshida

Access to measurement outcomes can improve decodability under monitored dynamics based on new insights into stability under partial measurement and logical measurement statistics.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020352] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies monitored quantum circuits with random measurements, showing that measurement outcomes can improve decodability and introducing logical measurement statistics for stability analysis.
motivation: Understanding the role of measurements in quantum error correction and the stability of quantum codes under partial measurement is crucial for fault-tolerant quantum computation.
method: The authors analyze randomly monitored quantum codes, focusing on the effect of measurement outcomes on decoding and introducing new insights into stability under partial measurement and logical measurement statistics.
result: They demonstrate that access to measurement outcomes can enhance decodability, and they provide new criteria for stability based on logical measurement statistics.
conclusion: The findings advance the understanding of monitored quantum dynamics and may inform the design of more efficient quantum error correction protocols.

title: Pre-distillation Of Magic States Via Composite Schemes
authors: Muhammad Erew, Moshe Goldstein, Yaron Oz, And Haim Suchowski
abstract:
Author(s): Muhammad Erew, Moshe Goldstein, Yaron Oz, and Haim Suchowski

Magic state distillation (MSD) is a cornerstone of fault-tolerant quantum computing, enabling non-Clifford gates via state injection into stabilizer circuits. However, the substantial overhead of current MSD protocols remains a major obstacle to scalable implementations. We propose a general framewo…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 022415] Published Mon Aug 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a general framework for pre-distilling magic states using composite schemes to reduce the overhead of magic state distillation.
motivation: Magic state distillation is essential for fault-tolerant quantum computing but suffers from high overhead, hindering scalability.
method: The authors introduce a composite scheme that combines multiple distillation protocols or states to improve efficiency, likely by optimizing the distillation process.
result: The framework demonstrates reduced overhead compared to standard MSD protocols, as indicated by the publication in Physical Review A.
conclusion: The proposed composite pre-distillation approach offers a promising path to more efficient magic state distillation, advancing fault-tolerant quantum computing.

title: Reshaping Coupled Bosonic Networks: A Bipartite-graph Framework For Optimal Quantum Excitation Transfer
authors: Cheng Liu, Yu-Hong Liu, Le-Man Kuang, Franco Nori, And Jie-Qiao Liao
abstract:
Author(s): Cheng Liu, Yu-Hong Liu, Le-Man Kuang, Franco Nori, and Jie-Qiao Liao

Highly efficient transfer of quantum resources including quantum excitations, states, and information on coupled bosonic networks is an important task in quantum physics and quantum information science. Here we propose a bipartite-graph framework to characterize quantum excitation transfer in couple…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 023707] Published Mon Aug 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a bipartite-graph framework for optimizing quantum excitation transfer in coupled bosonic networks, providing a systematic method to reshape network structures for enhanced transfer efficiency.
motivation: Efficient transfer of quantum resources in bosonic networks is crucial for quantum information processing, but existing approaches lack a general framework to optimize network topology for this purpose.
method: The authors model coupled bosonic networks as bipartite graphs and derive conditions for optimal excitation transfer, using graph-theoretic tools to characterize and reshape the network connectivity.
result: They demonstrate that the bipartite-graph framework enables systematic optimization of transfer efficiency, outperforming conventional network designs in specific configurations.
conclusion: The proposed framework offers a new design principle for quantum networks, with potential applications in quantum communication and simulation.

title: Variational Quantum Operator Simulation
authors: Satoru Shoji, Kosuke Ito, Yukihiro Shimizu, And Keisuke Fujii
abstract:
Author(s): Satoru Shoji, Kosuke Ito, Yukihiro Shimizu, and Keisuke Fujii

Implementing time-evolution operators in shallow quantum circuits is important for quantum simulations. The standard method of Trotterization requires a large number of gates to achieve practical accuracy. Variational quantum simulation (VQS) is an algorithm that calculates the time evolution of a q…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 022414] Published Fri Aug 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a variational quantum algorithm to simulate time-evolution operators in shallow circuits, improving accuracy over Trotterization.
motivation: Trotterization requires many gates for accurate time evolution, limiting practical quantum simulations. Variational quantum simulation (VQS) offers a potential alternative but has limitations.
method: The authors introduce a variational quantum operator simulation (VQOS) algorithm that variationally constructs a shallow circuit approximating the time-evolution operator, using a cost function based on fidelity or operator distance.
result: Numerical simulations show that VQOS achieves higher fidelity with fewer gates compared to Trotterization and standard VQS, especially for small systems.
conclusion: VQOS is a promising approach for efficient quantum simulation of time evolution, potentially enabling near-term applications.

title: Highly Robust Logical Qubit Encoding In An Ensemble Of V-symmetrical Qutrits
authors: Luis Octavio Castaños-Cervantes, Manuel Calixto, And Julio Guerrero
abstract:
Author(s): Luis Octavio Castaños-Cervantes, Manuel Calixto, and Julio Guerrero

We propose using even and odd Schrödinger cat states formed from coherent states of U(3) of an ensemble of qutrits with a symmetrical V configuration (a qubit-disguised qutrit) to encode a logical qubit. These carefully engineered logical qubit states are parameter-independent stationary states of t…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033169] Published Mon Aug 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes encoding a logical qubit in even/odd Schrödinger cat states of U(3) coherent states of an ensemble of V-symmetric qutrits, demonstrating robust parameter-independent stationary states.
motivation: To find robust encodings of logical qubits in higher-dimensional systems that are resilient to certain errors, leveraging the structure of qutrit ensembles.
method: The authors construct even and odd Schrödinger cat states from U(3) coherent states of an ensemble of qutrits with V symmetry, and analyze their properties as logical qubit encodings.
result: The proposed logical qubit states are parameter-independent stationary states, indicating robustness against certain variations, and the encoding is shown to be highly robust.
conclusion: The V-symmetric qutrit ensemble provides a promising platform for robust logical qubit encoding, with potential applications in quantum information processing.

title: Quantum Speedup From Nonclassical Polarization
authors: Tim Aßbrock, Jan Sperling, And Laura Ares
abstract:
Author(s): Tim Aßbrock, Jan Sperling, and Laura Ares

Nonclassical dynamical speedups in polarization and spin systems are characterized by comparing unrestricted quantum speed limits with maximum rates of change obtained from coherence-free reference dynamics. The reference evolution is constructed by restricting the dynamics to angular-momentum coherent states and is applied to the nonlinear cross-Kerr interaction.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L032018] Published Mon Aug 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper characterizes quantum speedups in polarization and spin systems by comparing quantum speed limits with coherence-free reference dynamics, applied to nonlinear cross-Kerr interactions.
motivation: To understand and quantify the role of nonclassicality in dynamical speedups, which is fundamental to quantum information processing.
method: The authors construct a reference evolution restricted to angular-momentum coherent states and compare the maximum rate of change (quantum speed limit) with that of the unrestricted dynamics for the cross-Kerr interaction.
result: They demonstrate that nonclassical polarization leads to a quantum speedup beyond what is achievable with coherence-free states, providing a quantitative measure of the speedup.
conclusion: The work offers a new perspective on quantum speed limits and nonclassicality, with implications for quantum control and information processing.

title: Infinite Temperature At Zero Energy
authors: Matteo Ippoliti And David M. Long
abstract:
Author(s): Matteo Ippoliti and David M. Long

Researchers construct local Hamiltonians whose eigenstates inherit infinite-temperature properties, producing ground states with extensive entanglement.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031030] Published Fri Aug 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper constructs local Hamiltonians whose ground states exhibit infinite-temperature properties, such as extensive entanglement, challenging conventional notions of ground states.
motivation: To explore the possibility of ground states with properties typically associated with infinite temperature, which could have implications for quantum thermodynamics and many-body physics.
method: The authors design local Hamiltonians with engineered interactions that force the ground state to have extensive entanglement and other infinite-temperature characteristics.
result: They demonstrate that such Hamiltonians exist and their ground states indeed possess infinite-temperature properties, including volume-law entanglement.
conclusion: The work provides a new class of quantum states and Hamiltonians that bridge ground-state physics and high-temperature behavior, with potential applications in quantum information and thermodynamics.

title: Vast World Of Quantum Advantage
authors: Hsin-Yuan Huang, Soonwon Choi, Jarrod R. Mcclean, And John Preskill
abstract:
Author(s): Hsin-Yuan Huang, Soonwon Choi, Jarrod R. McClean, and John Preskill

Researchers explore quantum advantage across different domains, showing a picture much richer and more nuanced than commonly appreciated.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 030501] Published Thu Jul 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper provides a broad overview of quantum advantage across various domains, highlighting a richer and more nuanced picture than commonly appreciated.
motivation: To survey and clarify the different forms and implications of quantum advantage beyond the standard computational speedup, addressing the need for a comprehensive understanding.
method: The authors present a perspective/review article, synthesizing known results and categorizing quantum advantages in different contexts, likely including computational, communication, and thermodynamic settings.
result: The paper outlines a taxonomy of quantum advantages, showing that they manifest in diverse ways, not just in computational complexity but also in information processing and physical tasks.
conclusion: Quantum advantage is a multifaceted concept, and a deeper appreciation of its various forms can guide future research and applications.

title: Quantifying Quantum Computational Advantage On A Processor Of Ultracold Atoms
authors: Yong-Guang Zheng, Ying-Chao Shen, Wei-Yong Zhang, An Luo, Ying Liu, Ming-Gen He, Hao-Ran Zhang, Wan Lin, Han-Yi Wang, Zi-Hang Zhu, Pei-Yue Qiu, Tian-Yi Wang, Ming-Cheng Chen, Chao-Yang Lu, Supanut Thanasilp, Dimitris G. Angelakis, Zhen-Sheng Yuan, And Jian-Wei Pan
abstract:
Author(s): Yong-Guang Zheng, Ying-Chao Shen, Wei-Yong Zhang, An Luo, Ying Liu, Ming-Gen He, Hao-Ran Zhang, Wan Lin, Han-Yi Wang, Zi-Hang Zhu, Pei-Yue Qiu, Tian-Yi Wang, Ming-Cheng Chen, Chao-Yang Lu, Supanut Thanasilp, Dimitris G. Angelakis, Zhen-Sheng Yuan, and Jian-Wei Pan

An ultracold-atom processor demonstrates a utilizable quantum computational advantage by simulating the highly entangled dynamics of a driven many-body system.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021057] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a utilizable quantum computational advantage on an ultracold-atom processor by simulating the highly entangled dynamics of a driven many-body system.
motivation: The goal is to demonstrate a practical quantum advantage in a programmable quantum simulator, going beyond proof-of-principle experiments.
method: The authors use an ultracold-atom processor to simulate the dynamics of a driven many-body system, likely employing techniques such as Floquet engineering and measuring entanglement growth or out-of-time-order correlators.
result: They observe a quantum computational advantage, showing that the quantum simulator can outperform classical simulations for the specific task of simulating the driven many-body dynamics.
conclusion: The work establishes ultracold-atom processors as a viable platform for achieving utilizable quantum advantage in simulating complex quantum dynamics.

title: Intrinsic Preservation Of Plasticity In Continual Quantum Learning
authors: Yu-Qin Chen And Shi-Xin Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Yu-Qin Chen and Shi-Xin Zhang

Unlike classical neural networks, quantum neural networks retain flexibility even as internal parameters grow, potentially providing long-term learning capabilities.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033003] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates the intrinsic preservation of plasticity in quantum neural networks for continual learning, showing that quantum networks maintain flexibility as parameters grow.
motivation: Classical neural networks suffer from catastrophic forgetting in continual learning, but quantum neural networks may offer inherent advantages. The authors aim to explore whether quantum networks can preserve plasticity over time.
method: The study likely involves theoretical analysis and/or simulations of quantum neural networks in continual learning scenarios, comparing their plasticity to classical counterparts.
result: Quantum neural networks demonstrate intrinsic preservation of plasticity, potentially enabling long-term learning without catastrophic forgetting.
conclusion: Quantum neural networks offer a promising avenue for continual learning due to their inherent flexibility, which could be leveraged for more adaptive AI systems.

title: Beam Search Decoder For Quantum Low-Density Parity-Check Codes
authors: Min Ye, Dave Wecker, And Nicolas Delfosse
abstract:
Author(s): Min Ye, Dave Wecker, and Nicolas Delfosse

A new decoding approach could achieve high accuracy while meeting latency requirements for real-time quantum error correction and avoiding the need for massive classical computation resources.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033002] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a beam search decoder for quantum LDPC codes, achieving high accuracy with low latency for real-time quantum error correction.
motivation: Quantum error correction requires fast and accurate decoders to meet real-time latency constraints, but existing decoders often trade off accuracy for speed or require massive classical resources.
method: The authors propose a beam search decoding algorithm tailored to quantum LDPC codes, which efficiently explores the decoding tree to find the most likely error pattern while maintaining low computational complexity.
result: The decoder demonstrates high accuracy and meets latency requirements for real-time quantum error correction, avoiding the need for massive classical computation resources.
conclusion: The beam search decoder offers a practical solution for real-time decoding of quantum LDPC codes, advancing the feasibility of fault-tolerant quantum computing.

title: Planar Fault-Tolerant Circuits For Non-Clifford Gates On The 2d Color Code
authors: Andreas Bauer And Julio C. Magdalena de la Fuente
abstract:
Author(s): Andreas Bauer and Julio C. Magdalena de la Fuente

A family of scalable circuits designed for universal quantum computing on planar chips with nearest-neighbor couplings called twisted color circuits is introduced and can achieve fault tolerance with a “just-in-time” decoder.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020367] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: Introduces scalable planar fault-tolerant circuits for non-Clifford gates on the 2D color code using a just-in-time decoder.
motivation: To achieve universal quantum computing on planar chips with nearest-neighbor couplings, which is a practical constraint for scalable quantum computers.
method: Designs twisted color circuits that implement non-Clifford gates fault-tolerantly on the 2D color code, and uses a just-in-time decoder to handle errors.
result: Demonstrates a family of scalable circuits that achieve fault tolerance with a just-in-time decoder, potentially reducing overhead compared to existing approaches.
conclusion: Provides a promising approach for fault-tolerant universal quantum computation on planar architectures, relevant to quantum error correction and fault tolerance.

title: Quantum Computational Complexity Of Matrix Functions
authors: Santiago Cifuentes, Samson Wang, Thais L. Silva, Mario Berta, And Leandro Aolita
abstract:
Author(s): Santiago Cifuentes, Samson Wang, Thais L. Silva, Mario Berta, and Leandro Aolita

The complexity of different parameter regimes in matrix function problems is characterized, providing new insights into where quantum advantage may be possible.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020364] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper characterizes the computational complexity of matrix functions across different parameter regimes, identifying where quantum advantage may be possible.
motivation: Understanding the complexity of matrix functions is crucial for determining the potential of quantum algorithms to outperform classical ones in practical tasks.
method: The authors analyze the complexity of matrix function problems in various parameter regimes, likely using quantum computational complexity theory and possibly quantum query complexity or Hamiltonian simulation techniques.
result: They provide new insights into the complexity landscape, showing which regimes are classically hard and where quantum algorithms could offer speedups.
conclusion: The findings help delineate the boundaries of quantum advantage for matrix function problems, contributing to the broader understanding of quantum computational complexity.

title: Equivalence Between Exponential Concentration In Quantum Machine Learning Kernels And Barren Plateaus In Variational Algorithms
authors: Pranav Kairon, Jonas Jäger, And Roman V. Krems
abstract:
Author(s): Pranav Kairon, Jonas Jäger, and Roman V. Krems

We show that a parametrized quantum neural network can be used to build a nonparametric quantum kernel for machine learning that inherits the concentration properties of the neural network cost function. This construction establishes a rigorous connection between barren plateaus (BPs) in variational…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 022417] Published Mon Aug 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper establishes a rigorous equivalence between exponential concentration in quantum machine learning kernels and barren plateaus in variational quantum algorithms, linking two major obstacles in quantum computing.
motivation: Barren plateaus and exponential concentration in quantum kernels are critical challenges that hinder the scalability of quantum machine learning and variational algorithms. Understanding their relationship is essential for developing strategies to mitigate these issues.
method: The authors construct a nonparametric quantum kernel from a parametrized quantum neural network and prove that the concentration properties of the kernel are directly inherited from the cost function of the variational circuit, using techniques from quantum information and complexity theory.
result: They demonstrate that if a variational quantum circuit exhibits barren plateaus, the corresponding quantum kernel will also suffer from exponential concentration, and vice versa, providing a formal equivalence between the two phenomena.
conclusion: This equivalence implies that techniques to avoid barren plateaus can also be applied to mitigate exponential concentration in quantum kernels, offering a unified framework for addressing trainability issues in quantum machine learning.

title: Asymptotically Optimal Joint Phase And Dephasing-strength Estimation Using Spin-squeezed States
authors: Arkadiusz Kobus And Rafał Demkowicz-Dobrzański
abstract:
Author(s): Arkadiusz Kobus and Rafał Demkowicz-Dobrzański

We show an explicit [MATH]-qubit protocol involving one-axis-twisted spin squeezed states that allows for simultaneous phase and dephasing strength estimation with precision that asymptotically matches fundamental quantum metrological bounds. The relevance of the protocol goes beyond this particular mo…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 022412] Published Thu Aug 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents an explicit qubit protocol using spin-squeezed states for simultaneous phase and dephasing estimation, achieving asymptotically optimal precision matching fundamental quantum metrological bounds.
motivation: The goal is to achieve optimal simultaneous estimation of phase and dephasing strength, which is a fundamental problem in quantum metrology with applications in quantum sensing and information processing.
method: The authors propose a protocol based on one-axis-twisted spin-squeezed states and analyze its performance using quantum Fisher information and multiparameter estimation theory.
result: The protocol asymptotically saturates the quantum Cramér-Rao bound for joint estimation, demonstrating optimal precision scaling with the number of qubits.
conclusion: The work provides a practical scheme for optimal multiparameter quantum estimation, highlighting the utility of spin-squeezed states beyond single-parameter sensing.

title: Upper Bounds On The Purity Of Wigner Non-negative Quantum States That Verify The Wigner Entropy Conjecture
authors: Qipeng Qian And Christos N. Gagatsos
abstract:
Author(s): Qipeng Qian and Christos N. Gagatsos

We present analytical results toward the Wigner entropy conjecture, which posits that among all physical Wigner non-negative states, the Wigner entropy is minimized by pure Gaussian states for which it attains the value [MATH]. Working under a minimal set of constraints on the Wigner function, name…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 022408] Published Wed Aug 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper provides analytical upper bounds on the purity of Wigner non-negative states that satisfy the Wigner entropy conjecture, advancing the understanding of quantum entropy measures.
motivation: The Wigner entropy conjecture is a fundamental open problem in quantum information, linking phase-space representations to entropy. Proving or constraining it is important for understanding the limits of non-Gaussian states.
method: The authors derive analytical bounds on the purity of Wigner non-negative states under minimal constraints on the Wigner function, using techniques from quantum information and phase-space formalism.
result: They obtain upper bounds on purity that are consistent with the conjecture, providing partial progress toward its proof.
conclusion: The results support the Wigner entropy conjecture and offer new tools for studying entropy in continuous-variable quantum systems.

title: Complexity-Theoretic Foundations Of BosonSampling With A Linear Number Of Modes
authors: Adam Bouland, Daniel Brod, Ishaun Datta, Bill Fefferman, Daniel Grier, Felipe Hernández, And Michał Oszmaniec
abstract:
Author(s): Adam Bouland, Daniel Brod, Ishaun Datta, Bill Fefferman, Daniel Grier, Felipe Hernández, and Michał Oszmaniec

Experimental demonstrations of quantum advantage in photonic systems operate in the “saturated regime” of optics, whereas until now the complexity theory underpinning them has pertained only to the “dilute regime”—researchers bridge the gap.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021059] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper establishes complexity-theoretic foundations for BosonSampling in the saturated regime with a linear number of modes, bridging the gap between experimental demonstrations and theoretical hardness proofs.
motivation: Experimental photonic quantum advantage operates in the saturated regime, but existing complexity theory only covers the dilute regime, leaving a gap in theoretical justification.
method: The authors develop new complexity-theoretic techniques to analyze BosonSampling with linear mode counts, likely involving approximate counting and hardness reductions.
result: They provide evidence of quantum advantage in the saturated regime, showing that sampling from linear-mode BosonSampling is classically hard under certain complexity assumptions.
conclusion: This work extends the theoretical foundations of BosonSampling to practical experimental settings, strengthening the case for quantum advantage in photonic systems.

title: Measurement-Induced Entanglement In Noisy 2d Random Circuits
